title: Tame equivariant Cohen–Gabber for a reduced equidimensional ring
statement: Let $(C,\mathfrak n)$ be a reduced complete Noetherian local ring of characteristic $p>0$, equidimensional of dimension $e\geq1$, with residue field $k=C/\mathfrak n$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Reduced means no nonzero nilpotents, and equidimensional means $\dim(C/\mathfrak q)=e$ for every minimal prime $\mathfrak q$. Let a finite group $H$ act on $C$ by local ring automorphisms, with $|H|$ invertible in $k$. There exist an $H$-equivariant field section $s:k\hookrightarrow C$ of the residue map and $H$-fixed elements $u_1,\ldots,u_e\in\mathfrak n$ such that the continuous evaluation map $k[[T_1,\ldots,T_e]]\to C$, with coefficient map $s$ and $T_i\mapsto u_i$, is injective, local, module-finite and torsion free, and induces the identity on residue fields [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The radical of $(u_1,\ldots,u_e)C$ is $\mathfrak n$. For $K=\operatorname{Frac}(k[[T_1,\ldots,T_e]])$, the generic algebra $C\otimes_{k[[T]]}K$ is a finite product of finite separable extensions of $K$ [def-weil-module-base-change] [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Here $H$ acts on $k$ through the residue action and fixes every $T_i$. If an $H$-stable perfect subfield $k_0\subseteq C$ is specified, $s$ restricts to its given inclusion after identifying $k_0$ with its residue image; perfect means that $x\mapsto x^p$ is bijective.

source.place: Exposé IV Theorem 2.2.2 and proof 2.2.4–2.2.6, pp.53–55, restricted to the equidimensional case; generic separability is the generically étale assertion. Compatibility with a perfect subfield is the unique compatible p-power-root argument of IV 2.1.4.

proof.text: Put $B=C^H$ and $\mathfrak n=B\cap\mathfrak m_C$. Apply [lem-per-tame-fixed-ring-generic-components]. Thus $B$ is reduced complete Noetherian local, equidimensional of dimension $e$, with residue field $\lambda=k^H$; $C$ is finite over $B$ and $k/\lambda$ is finite separable. Every minimal $\mathfrak q$ of $C$ contracts to a minimal $\mathfrak r$ of $B$, and $L_{\mathfrak q}=\operatorname{Frac}(C/\mathfrak q)$ is finite separable over $M_{\mathfrak r}=\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak r)$. These assertions allow the non-equivariant construction on $B$, rather than making a choice of parameters on $C$ and trying to average them.

source.place: IV 2.2.3–2.2.4, printed pp.53–54; equidimensional case, so the maximal equidimensional quotient of 2.2.4 is B itself.

proof.text: By [lem-per-coefficient-field-generic-differential-basis], choose a coefficient section $t:\lambda\hookrightarrow B$ and $a_1,\ldots,a_e\in\mathfrak n$ whose differentials form a basis of $\widehat\Omega_{B/\lambda}\otimes_B M_{\mathfrak r}$ for every minimal $\mathfrak r$. Choose $\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_e\in\mathfrak n$ with $\sqrt{(\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_e)B}=\mathfrak n$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-system-of-parameters]. Define $u_i=\tau_i^p(1+a_i)$. Since $1+a_i$ is a unit, a prime contains every $u_i$ exactly when it contains every $\tau_i$, so $\sqrt{(u_1,\ldots,u_e)B}=\mathfrak n$. Apply case (a) of [lem-per-parameter-ideal-formal-normalization] with this section and tuple: $R_0=\lambda[[T_1,\ldots,T_e]]\to B$ is injective, local, finite and torsion free. For $K_0=\operatorname{Frac}(R_0)$, it gives $B\otimes_{R_0}K_0=\prod_{\mathfrak r}M_{\mathfrak r}$ with every factor finite over $K_0$.

source.place: IV 2.1.4–2.1.12, especially the explicit formula t_i = τ_i^p(1+f_i) in 2.1.12; IV 2.2.4 applies this construction to the fixed ring.

proof.text: The universal derivation satisfies $\mathrm d(u_i)=\tau_i^p\mathrm da_i$: the Leibniz rule gives $\mathrm d(\tau_i^p)=p\tau_i^{p-1}\mathrm d\tau_i=0$ in characteristic $p$. None of the $\tau_i$ belongs to a minimal $\mathfrak r$: case (a) of [lem-per-parameter-ideal-formal-normalization], now applied to the original tuple $\tau$, makes $B$ torsion free over $\lambda[[\tau]]$ and identifies its generic algebra with $\prod M_{\mathfrak r}$, so every variable has nonzero image in every factor. Consequently the $\mathrm du_i$ remain a basis on each $M_{\mathfrak r}$. The exact sequence [lem-per-finite-formal-map-differential-cokernel] for $R_0\to B$, tensored with $M_{\mathfrak r}$ using [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], gives $\Omega_{B/R_0}\otimes_B M_{\mathfrak r}=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization], localization at the nonzero elements of $B/\mathfrak r$ is not being assumed: instead first localize $B$ at $R_0\setminus\{0\}$, obtaining the displayed product of fields, and then project to the factor $M_{\mathfrak r}$. Projection to a field factor is localization at its idempotent, so the same node identifies the resulting module with $\Omega_{M_{\mathfrak r}/R_0}$. Every $R_0$-derivation on this field annihilates $K_0$: $D(s^{-1})=-s^{-2}D(s)=0$ for $s\in R_0\setminus\{0\}$. The universal property [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] therefore identifies this with $\Omega_{M_{\mathfrak r}/K_0}=0$. Each finite field extension $M_{\mathfrak r}/K_0$ is separable by [lem-weil-pbc-fg-field-zero-differentials-separable].

source.place: IV 2.1.12, printed pp.52–53, exact sequence and calculation of d(t_i); localization of differentials is Stacks Tag 00RT (algebra-lemma-differentials-localize).

proof.text: Lift the coefficient field as in IV 2.2.6. The complete ring $C$ is henselian by [lem-weil-pbc-complete-pair-henselian]. Choose $\alpha$ with $k=\lambda(\alpha)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-primitive-element], and let $P\in\lambda[X]$ be its monic minimal polynomial. Regard its coefficients in $C$ via $t$. Its reduction has the simple root $\alpha$ in $k$, since $k/\lambda$ is separable. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting] there is a root $b\in C$ reducing to $\alpha$. Using [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-polynomial-quotient-field-iso], evaluation $X\mapsto b$ defines a unital map $s:k=\lambda[X]/(P)\to C$. It is injective since $k$ is a field and $C$ is nonzero; its residue composite fixes both $\lambda$ and $\alpha$, hence is the identity. Any other $\lambda$-algebra section takes $\alpha$ to a root of $P$ with the same residue and invertible derivative, hence to $b$ by [lem-weil-pbc-simple-root-uniqueness]. Thus $s$ is the unique such section. For $h\in H$, the map $h\circ s\circ\bar h^{-1}:k\to C$ is again a $\lambda$-algebra residue section, since $t(\lambda)\subseteq B$ is fixed and $\bar h$ fixes $\lambda$. Uniqueness gives $h\circ s=s\circ\bar h$.

source.place: IV 2.2.6, printed p.55; explicit primitive-element Hensel lift. Supporting Stacks Tags 0ALJ, 030N, 04GG, 09G1 and 06RR.

proof.text: The $u_i$ lie in $B$ and are therefore $H$-fixed. The finite extension $B\to C$ is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. If a prime $\mathfrak q\subset C$ contains all $u_i$, its contraction contains their ideal in $B$ and hence equals $\mathfrak n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal], $\mathfrak q$ is maximal, hence equals $\mathfrak m_C$. This proves $\sqrt{(u_1,\ldots,u_e)C}=\mathfrak m_C$. Apply case (a) of [lem-per-parameter-ideal-formal-normalization] to $C$, the coefficient section $s$ and this tuple. It gives precisely the injective local module-finite torsion-free evaluation map $R=k[[T_1,\ldots,T_e]]\to C$ with identity residue map, and $C\otimes_R K=\prod_{\mathfrak q}L_{\mathfrak q}$, each factor finite over $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$. Evaluation is continuous: $(T_1,\ldots,T_e)^N$ maps into $\mathfrak m_C^N$. The action on series is coefficientwise and fixes variables; evaluating a truncated series commutes with $h$ by coefficient equivariance and fixedness of $u_i$. The difference for a full series lies in every $\mathfrak m_C^N$, hence is zero by [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Thus the evaluation map is $H$-equivariant.

source.place: IV 2.2.4–2.2.6, formal evaluation and finiteness; Stacks 00GK and 00GS for extending the parameter ideal.

proof.text: For a minimal $\mathfrak q$ of $C$, put $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak q\cap B$. The fields form a tower $K_0\subset M_{\mathfrak r}\subset L_{\mathfrak q}$ in which the first extension is separable by Step 3 and the second by Step 1. By [lem-zl-separable-permanence], $L_{\mathfrak q}/K_0$ is separable. The coefficient map $s$ extends $t$ and the variables have the same images, so the injection $R\hookrightarrow L_{\mathfrak q}$ from Step 5 restricts to the injection $R_0\hookrightarrow M_{\mathfrak r}$ from Step 2. Passing to fractions gives $K_0\subset K\subset L_{\mathfrak q}$. By [lem-sfb-separable-algebraic-intermediate-base], $L_{\mathfrak q}/K$ is separable; it is finite by Step 5. The product in Step 5 is therefore the required finite product of finite separable extensions. This uses generic separability of the fixed-ring quotient, rather than assuming the separability of the two evaluation maps is automatic.

source.place: IV 2.2.6, last sentence; Stacks Tags 09HB (fields-lemma-separable-permanence) and 09H2 (fields-lemma-separable-goes-up).

proof.text: Finally suppose that the specified perfect subfield $k_0\subseteq C$ is present. For $a\in k_0$ and each $N$, choose $a_N\in k_0$ with $a_N^{p^N}=a$. Then $s(\overline{a_N})-a_N\in\mathfrak m_C$. By [def-weil-ring-frobenius], $s(\bar a)-a=(s(\overline{a_N})-a_N)^{p^N}\in\mathfrak m_C^{p^N}$. Separation in [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] makes this difference zero. Thus every residue section, in particular the equivariant section constructed above, respects the prescribed perfect subfield. This argument works when $H$ acts nontrivially on $k_0$ and does not require $k_0\subset B$.

source.place: IV 2.1.4, compatibility of coefficient representatives with compatible p-power roots, written out.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NX-548177684 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, its 7 steps, the new node and all 20 cited statements, and checked them against ILO IV 2.1.12 and IV 2.2.2–2.2.6 (printed pp.52–55). This is the item's first split; the statement is unchanged from the base. Step 1: the new node lem-per-tame-fixed-ring-generic-components states ILO IV 2.2.3 and 2.2.4 for B = C^H. It is true: Reynolds averaging gives Noetherian, local, residue field k^H and complete; C/nC is Artinian and finite over λ, so C is finite over B; minimal primes contract to minimal primes by lying-over, going-up and conjugacy; the generic fields satisfy M_r = L_q^{D_q}, a Galois extension. It does not restate the item and it is not a duplicate: tame-admissible-scheme-quotient gives only finiteness and Noetherianity. Step 2: the coefficient-field, system-of-parameters and parameter-normalization (a) hypotheses all hold on B, and u_i = τ_i^p(1+a_i) has the same radical as τ. Step 3: d u_i = τ_i^p d a_i. τ_i is a nonzerodivisor (torsion-free over λ[[τ]]), so it lies in no minimal prime. The exact sequence plus right exactness give Ω⊗M_r = 0; localizing at R0∖0 and then at the factor idempotent, plus 090W, gives M_r/K0 separable. Step 4: the Hensel simple-root lift of a primitive element gives a unique λ-section s, which is therefore H-equivariant, as in ILO 2.2.6. Step 5: by integrality rad(uC) = m_C, and case (a) on C gives every clause of the item; equivariance follows by truncation. Step 6: separability passes up the tower K0 ⊂ M_r ⊂ L_q and then over K (09HB, 09H2). Step 7: the p^N-th power argument makes every section compatible with the perfect subfield k0. I tested k[[x,y]]/(xy) with the swap, trivial H and e = 1. lean.note: The auxiliary predicate expands exactly the promised presentation clauses; its target algebra structure is f.toAlgebra. Coefficients, variables, and ideal-power continuity characterize the evaluation map uniquely.
